findings.title: get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty
findings.body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data the code initializes counter_updates={} and only populates it inside `if self.counter_names:`. It then unconditionally does `counter_updates[gk]` when building DetectorStateData. If a detector implements `counter_names` as [] (no counters to track), the dict stays empty and the lookup raises KeyError, crashing evaluation for every group_key. The fallback should be an empty dict or dict of Nones per group_key.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler became abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (which only required `evaluate`, which it implemented) to StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. With no implementations the subclass remains abstract, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` via `Detector.detector_handler` raises TypeError. The previous version returned [] and was instantiable; this is a regression for any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`.

findings.title: get_group_key_values type excludes None group_key
findings.body: The abstract signature is `-> dict[str, int]` but `DetectorGroupKey` is `str | None` and the codebase routinely uses `None` as a group_key (tests use `{None: 6}`, `build_dedupe_value_key` explicitly handles `None`). The annotation is wrong and hides None-handling requirements from implementers and type checkers. It should be `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`.

findings.title: Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` but its docstring still says it “returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult”. Readers relying on the docstring will expect list semantics instead of dict keyed by group_key.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores value so wrong forwarding is not caught
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event takes `value: int` but never uses it, and TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with value 6 while the data packet contains group_2:10. Because the helper ignores the argument the tests pass regardless of what `value` StatefulDetectorHandler passes to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. A bug that swaps or mis-forwards group values would not be detected.
